entry.title: Collaborative paper with David lab online!

link.title: Collaborative paper with David lab online!

entry.content: A collaborative paper with the David Lab is online now at JACS. Abi led the biophysical modeling of amino acid residues on SRSF2 that destabilize the native protein-RNA complex upon glycation. Congrats to Abi!

entry.title: Pershing Square prize!
entry.content: Caleb is among the national winners of the 2026 Pershing Square Sohn Prize for Cancer Research. This award supports new directions for the lab to engineer proteins for potential therapeutic use.

entry.title: New preprints!
entry.content: The lab releases two new preprints! First, the lab introduces GIFT, a scalable genotyping platform for single-cell lineage tracing. The second preprint is on HSV-1 reactivation in the brain, implicating a population of RORB+ neurons as a potential reservoir of herpesvirus latency and reactivation that may trigger dementias, including Alzheimer’s disease. Congratulations to Austin, Jacob, Benan, and Laura on the great work!

entry.title: Second annual human virome meeting
entry.content: Caleb, Sherry, Cole, Jacob, and Erin attend the 2nd annual Human Virome Program Meeting in Rockville, MD. The group discussed recent updates in their use of genomics technologies to map host-viral interactions, including single-cell profiling and population-scale data analysis.

entry.title: EBV DNA persistence paper online!
entry.content: Our manuscript describing the study of EBV persistence in population-scale biobanks is now online at Nature. This work establishes a new framework to study why and how human responses vary so dramatically following infection from the same endemic agent. Be sure to check out the accompanying News and Views. Congratulations to Sherry, Erin, Meghana, Laura, Hoyin, Jacob, and Thahmina for this outstanding work!

entry.title: First protein design paper online!
entry.content: The lab’s first paper on de novo protein design is out on bioRxiv. We screened over 1,500 new proteins for efficacy in binding and CAR T efficacy, discovering principles that inform how to make effective CAR T cells for a variety of surface antigens. Congrats to Arthur, Hoyin, Betty, Benan, Abi, and Laura for leading the lab in a new direction!

entry.title: New papers online!
entry.content: Several papers from our collaborative projects are now online! Led by the Alex Gitlin lab, new work provides a thorough mechanistic characterization of VEXAS Syndrome. In a shared effort with Payam Gammage and Ed Reznik, we help characterize functionally dominant hotspot mutations in mitochondrial ribosomal RNA. Finally, in a collaboration with Robbie Majzner’s group at Dana Farber, we defined how SLP-76 can be engineered to improve T cell fitness and antigen sensitivity. Thanks to Benan and Hoyin for helping with these collaborative efforts!

entry.title: National Academy of Medicine Catalyst
entry.content: The lab is awarded a Catalyst prize from the National Academy of Medicine for our continued work in defining the human virome. Thank you NAM for believing in our vision and supporting our work!
